title: Autonomous machine-learning experiments identify a dual-anion aqueous sodium electrolyte with a wider stability window
summary: A robotic electrochemistry stand coupled to Bayesian optimization tested 140 aqueous electrolyte formulas over 40 hours and selected a non-intuitive sodium mixture of NaClO4 and NaNO3. On platinum, the blend had a wider electrochemical stability window than the NaClO4 baseline despite lower total salt concentration; follow-up tests reported a 24 mV increase in the OER potential at the stated leakage-current criterion and 58% lower current density at 2 V. The result is a measured electrolyte formulation under the paper’s electrochemical protocols, not evidence of a commercial battery or field-ready cell.
ai_technology: Dragonfly Bayesian optimization software coupled to the Otto robotic electrochemistry test stand

evidence.tested: A robotic electrochemistry stand coupled to Bayesian optimization tested 140 aqueous electrolyte formulas over 40 hours and selected a non-intuitive sodium mixture of NaClO4 and NaNO3.
evidence.unknown: The study measured electrochemical behavior primarily on platinum electrodes and reports a wider stability window for the selected aqueous blend under its stated protocol. This does not establish long-term performance, commercial readiness, or general improvement across battery chemistries.
evidence.ai_role: Dragonfly selected electrolyte formulations sequentially from real-time measurements and guided autonomous experiment requests to Otto; the paper reports the mixed-anion sodium formulation as the optimization result.
